01 · Why Football

A $50bn market
driven by structural scarcity.

Football is one of the largest, most liquid and fastest-growing global sports markets. Crisis-resilient. AI-resistant. Structurally non-cyclical.

Capital moves late in football, driven by hype, urgency and fear of missing out. We operate early, before the market prices the asset.

+40%
Transfer value CAGR Average South American player transfer value grows at approximately 40% year over year. Source: private football market research.
$50B
Global football market Media rights, sponsorships, ticketing and player trading, a market that grew through multiple recessions and a global pandemic.
6+
Month value realisation cycles Short investment cycles with asymmetric upside. Entry at early-stage pricing, exit at international market pricing.
02 · Vision & Mission

The world's leading multi-club groups, City Football Group, Red Bull, and the new generation of European platforms, all face the same structural gap: access to South American talent at the source. Best Eleven is that missing piece: the supply base, already operating, in the region's three deepest talent markets.

The Mission

To make Best Eleven the global reference for the export of South American talent.

What European Multi-Club Groups Need
  • Early access to South American talent at the source
  • First-look rights before the market prices players
  • Local operating structures they cannot build alone
  • Regulatory-clean supply, no UEFA multi-club conflicts
  • Talent shaped to professional European standards
  • A trusted, institutional counterparty in the region
→
What Best Eleven Delivers
  • Operating clubs in Argentina, Paraguay & Uruguay
  • Proprietary scouting system: +11,000 active players monitored manually
  • The Semillero: a full talent production pipeline
  • Assets from 3rd division to Primera, full ladder coverage
  • 20+ years of relationship capital in football markets
  • Export-ready players for European platforms

European groups have built the destination: flagship clubs and bridge structures. What none of them has built is the source. Best Eleven is the South American supply engine, already operating, with proven exits and institutional relationships. What we are raising capital for is scale acceleration.

Player Production Pipeline
The Semillero Model

Investment in player development across Argentina, Uruguay, and Paraguay gives us early access to the region's best emerging talent. Early recruitment allows us to compete for the next generation of top players and shape them according to Best Eleven's methods, values, and conditioning infrastructure, before the market prices them.

The long-term goal: the greatest assets our clubs produce will not come from scouting. They will come from within: players developed entirely inside the Best Eleven ecosystem, export-ready for European multi-club platforms seeking first access to South American talent.

05 · Best Eleven Platform Value

The platform exists
before the capital arrives.

BESG is not a portfolio assembled through acquisition. It is an operating platform built over more than twenty years inside South American football.

Its foundations are institutional: standing relationships with club presidents, boards, sporting directors, federations, agents and coaching structures across three countries. Access of this kind is granted over time. It is not purchased.

The clubs in the platform were selected against a narrow mandate: financially stable, professionally managed, institutionally healthy, and free from political interference or organised supporter groups able to block long-term decisions. Assets meeting every condition are scarce, and identifying them requires operating inside the system rather than observing it from outside.

Capital can buy a football club.
It cannot buy the invitation to run one.
Twenty Years of Relationships
Two decades operating inside South American football, across club boards, federations, agents and coaching structures.
Institutional Trust
The founders were invited into these institutions before they invested in them. Boards open to parties they already know.
Curated Club Selection
Each club screened for financial stability, professional management and independence from political or supporter pressure.
Proven Execution
Management team, scouting methodology, international network and legal framework already operating across three countries, and structured to add further clubs without rebuilding it.
Difficult to Replicate
Comparable capital can finance the same assets. It cannot compress the years required to earn the same standing.

Key Assumptions
Conservative case assumes one fewer promotion, ~40% lower transfer realisation, and no Libertadores prize income before 2029. Even so, group revenue compounds to $15.7M by 2031: $15.2M from the clubs plus $0.5M of representation commissions, haircut on the same basis.

How the group total is built. At maturity each club's BESG-attributable revenue: Lito ~$11.8M × 100%, Colegiales ~$8.5M × 70% and Rubio Ñu ~$11.3M × 50%, or ~$23.4M. On top of the clubs, the representation agency adds ~$0.9M by 2031, taking the group total to ~$24.3M. The reduced shares apply only after each club's investment is recovered (targeted for the start of 2030). These figures are incremental: they reflect the additional revenue the investment generates, not the clubs’ full operations.

From revenue to profit. Steady-state squad budgets are deducted from that revenue: Lito USD 3M/year once in Primera and playing Libertadores, Colegiales USD 1M/year of extra salaries on promotion to Primera and Rubio Ñu USD 2.4M/year, which is $4.9M net of ownership shares. At Colegiales the Primera TV rights pay the base squad and are therefore excluded from group revenue. Deducting group overheads as well (USD 70K a month, $0.84M a year), the target case reaches ~$18.6M of profit and the conservative case ~$10M, which carries the same deduction even though Lito would not reach Primera in that scenario and its budget would be lower. The plan funds squad expansion on top of each club’s existing base, not the base itself.
12 · Risks & Mitigation

We've priced
the downside.

Football is volatile. The platform is built so that no single sporting outcome breaks the investment.

Sporting risk · relegation / no promotion
Mitigation: three clubs across three markets diversify outcomes. Real estate retains value independent of division. Conservative case assumes missed promotions.
Transfer-market & player risk
Mitigation: A dedicated scouting platform of 9 people, active 24/7, reaching the most remote talent hubs across South America. Pipeline, not one-off bets.
FX & macro (Argentina)
Mitigation: transfers and prize income are USD/EUR-denominated. Hard assets hold value in dollar terms; revenue is export-led.
Regulatory & governance
Mitigation: regulatory-clean structure with no UEFA multi-club conflicts. SAD in Uruguay; assembly-approved management agreements elsewhere.
Capital protection: ~$14M of the raise buys hard, appreciating real estate on the group balance sheet, a downside floor that exists regardless of any sporting result.
13 · Investment Proposal

The Ask.

Two ways to invest.

Same clubs, same operating team, same scouting platform. Choose how much of the capital goes into real estate versus pure sporting performance. Both plans include $2M in flexible player-investment opportunities, deployed over two years.

Option A Full Platform +
$22.5Mfor40%equity
Squad budgets plus real estate: stadiums, training facilities and land, building permanent BESG assets across all three clubs.
Accelerated waterfall: 70% of annual profit until the capital is returned.
View full breakdown →
Option B Sporting Performance
$9.2Mfor17.4%equity
Pure sporting capital: squad budgets, targeted training-facility improvements and founder milestones only. No real estate acquisition.
Accelerated waterfall: 70% of annual profit until the capital is returned.
View full breakdown →

Why the two plans are priced differently. Both deploy the same USD 8.5M of sporting capital: squad budgets across the three clubs and the player investment pool. Plan B adds USD 0.7M of improvements on rented facilities. Plan A instead commits USD 14M, 62% of the raise, to owned land, stadiums and training facilities. Those are permanent assets that appreciate and generate rent, but they return capital more slowly and in lower proportion than player trading. The entry valuation of each plan reflects that difference in the speed and the shape of the return, not a different view of what the platform is worth.

Accelerated distribution waterfall. The investor takes 70% of BESG's annual distributable profit ahead of any other distribution, until 100% of the USD 22.5M is back. On the deck's own projections that point is reached in 2031.

Use of Funds

Player acquisition, squad salaries and management agreements. Stadium and facility construction. Club operations and executive team across all markets.

Investment Structure

Equity in Best Eleven Sports Group (BESG). Direct participation in the group holding entity, not individual clubs. Full upside across all assets, all markets, all exit paths.

Governance & Asset Ownership

Full legal and contractual control of all clubs. Assembly-approved agreements in place. SAD structure in Uruguay. Facilities acquired or built by BESG are BESG assets, available to managed clubs under agreement but not club property. Exception: Colegiales stadium, which belongs to the club; BESG investment improves a shared asset.
